{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABdMJIHg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhGt06w", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 1, "title": "Add contributor templates, development/review/merge policies, UI/UX and test/CI principles, and AGENTS.md", "body": "## Problem

cognix currently has an empty initial commit and no shared contributor or AI guidance. Establish a coherent documentation and template baseline using recent managed repositories, especially 3dgs-viewer.

## Expected outcome

Add Issue/PR templates, development/review/merge policies, UI/UX and layout principles, test and CI performance principles, and a concise `AGENTS.md`. Adapt the references to cognix's actual state. Its product scope and implementation stack are not defined by this Issue.

## References

Use these as examples, adapting repository names, links, wording and actual tooling:

- [3dgs-viewer documentation index](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/README.md) and [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
- [3dgs-viewer Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md) and [PR template](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md)
- [3dgs-viewer development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review/merge guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)
- [3dgs-viewer UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/docs/ui-ux-principles.md) and [test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/3dgs-viewer/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md)
- [three-motionbricks development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and [test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/three-motionbricks/blob/main/docs/testing-ci-principles.md)
- [webgpu-devtools UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/webgpu-devtools/blob/main/README.md#uiux)

Do not import viewer-specific features, GPU/model requirements, historical Issue-specific restrictions, or commands that do not exist in cognix.

## Required changes

### Issue and PR templates

Add:

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md`
- `.github/pull_request_template.md`

Include the problem, expected outcome, context/reproduction, focused changes, related Issues, remaining scope, and validation actually performed.

Give mandatory acceptance criteria stable identifiers such as AC1 so PR evidence can map to every criterion. Separate **mandatory pre-merge acceptance**, **optional validation**, and **genuinely required post-merge verification**; allow “None required” where appropriate. Report Pass, Fail, Skipped and Not run accurately, with reasons for gaps. Pending CI is not a pass.

Use closing references only for a complete Issue resolution. A partial PR must use a non-closing reference, identify remaining work, and leave the source Issue open.

### Development, review and merge policies

Add `docs/development-flow.md` and `docs/review-guidelines.md`.

- Describe Issue → implementation → PR → review → revision → merge, with post-merge work only when actually required.
- Use **English** for newly authored repository documentation, AI guidance, templates, Issue/PR titles and bodies, reviews, and commit messages. The maintainer's chat language and product localization are unaffected.
- Prefer the smallest coherent change that fully satisfies the Issue. Check both omitted requirements and unnecessary additions; avoid speculative abstractions, unrelated refactors and unjustified frameworks/configuration.
- Assess every required Issue criterion against the actual current PR head. Return missing implementation, validation and other agent-fixable findings to the fix stage; do not silently redefine the work as a partial success.
- Permit an explicitly scoped partial integration under existing maintainer/workflow authorization while preserving unmet criteria and the open Issue. Partial integration does not establish full Issue completion.
- Separate genuine external blockers from agent-fixable defects. Record the concrete missing evidence/decision and resume condition; continue independent work.
- **Await pending CI instead of repeating unchanged reviews, publications or merge attempts.** Inspect failures and classify their actual causes before fixing or retrying. A completed result, changed code or resolved blocker can justify the next review.
- Preserve progress when blocked. Do not repeatedly request the same already-resolved decision or treat silence as agreement. Apply owner decisions only to their explicitly agreed scope.
- Do not invent completion gates, Issue-specific partial-only rules or mandatory human/device/private-data checks. Require human input or subjective approval only when the actual Issue needs it, with a reason and expected evidence.
- Merge only the reviewed current head after applicable mandatory checks pass, under the repository/workflow's existing authorization. Do not introduce a blanket new human-approval requirement or bypass required checks.
- Keep truly post-merge-only verification pending until performed. A merge-triggered deployment cannot be a pre-merge prerequisite.

### UI/UX and layout principles

Add one canonical `docs/ui-ux-principles.md`, applicable when user-facing interfaces are introduced.

- **Keep it simple; show, don't tell; make interaction intuitive and predictable.**
- Prioritize the user's main task/content/result and group controls near their effects.
- Use spacing, alignment, grouping and visual hierarchy; avoid redundant headings, repeated helper prose, decorative status messages and unnecessary panels.
- Keep everyday actions discoverable and expose advanced/contextual controls when relevant.
- Preserve responsive layouts, readable content, keyboard access, logical focus order, visible focus, accessible names, meaningful labels, actionable errors and useful recovery/progress feedback.
- Preserve necessary consent and destructive-action safeguards.
- Define general principles suitable for cognix without inventing its UI, prescribing a 3D-viewer layout or selecting a framework.

### Test and CI performance principles

Add `docs/testing-ci-principles.md` and link it from development and review guidance.

- Detect concrete defects at the lightest meaningful layer; use fast unit/component tests for appropriate logic and expensive integration/browser/device/service checks only for boundaries that require them.
- Match checks to the actual change and repository tooling. Documentation-only changes need documentation checks, without unrelated runtime suites or dependencies.
- Avoid tests that merely mirror implementation, equivalent duplicate checks, and automatic Cartesian products of formats, environments, inputs and states. Preserve necessary assertions and regression/integration confidence.
- Prefer small synthetic or appropriately licensed representative fixtures. Justify large datasets, repeated downloads and external-resource dependencies by concrete additional coverage.
- Reuse applicable builds/downloads with correct cache keys and isolation. Avoid equivalent push/PR validation for the same revision; cancel superseded work when safe.
- Choose parallelism from measured elapsed time/resource use. Distinguish fast feedback, required regression coverage, expensive exploratory checks and deployment responsibilities.
- Review new checks for additional defect coverage, duplication, runtime and maintenance cost. Establish repository-specific measured baselines/budgets when executable tooling exists and investigate growth.
- State current tooling honestly. Do not invent test/build commands, measured runtimes, results or executable CI that the repository does not have.

### AGENTS.md and navigation

Add a concise `AGENTS.md` linking the canonical development, review/merge, UI/UX/layout and test/CI guidance. Keep policy definitions in their canonical documents rather than duplicating conflicting copies.

Add a minimal truthful `README.md` index if needed, linking these guides and templates. Do not invent product features or setup instructions.

## Scope

This Issue adds documentation and templates. Product requirements, application implementation, language/framework selection, package/build scaffolding, executable tests/CI/deployment workflows, and unrelated policies belong in separately scoped work when needed. Add no dependency solely to validate this baseline.

## Mandatory pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **AC1:** Valid Issue template includes problem/outcome/context, identified criteria, and distinct mandatory/optional/post-merge validation.
- [ ] **AC2:** PR template maps evidence to every Issue criterion, reports actual statuses and remaining scope, and uses correct closing/non-closing references.
- [ ] **AC3:** Development guidance defines the workflow, English collaboration convention, focused complete implementation and checks appropriate to actual tooling.
- [ ] **AC4:** Review/merge guidance assesses the full Issue, distinguishes defects/blockers/pending CI, prevents unchanged loops, preserves existing authorization, and distinguishes accepted partial integration from full completion.
- [ ] **AC5:** Canonical UI/UX/layout principles cover the three core principles, task hierarchy, discoverability, responsive layout, accessibility and meaningful feedback without assuming an implementation.
- [ ] **AC6:** Canonical test/CI principles cover meaningful coverage, lightweight layers, change-based checks, fixtures/resources, caching/duplication, measured parallelism and runtime budgets.
- [ ] **AC7:** `AGENTS.md` and minimal README navigation link the canonical guides/templates; names, English terminology and local links are consistent and cognix-specific.
- [ ] **AC8:** Validate template metadata, Markdown structure, relative links and heading anchors, cross-document consistency and whitespace; run `git diff --check` and inspect the complete diff including new files. Record actual checks/results and any limitations.

## Optional validation

None required beyond applicable lightweight documentation checks.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. This baseline does not require a deployed application, live-site checks, human design approval or unrelated runtime execution.
